text.p: Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) may rise on Monday on recent news of the appointment of a new chairman of the exchange, brokers said.
Brokers said the market, dogged by a recent scandal over share price manipulation, would gain new impetus from the change.

Abdul Haq Howlader was named as the new chief by the DSE governing council at a meeting on Sunday, replacing Imtiyaz Husain. "The investors may come forward with fresh commitments when they see new faces in the bourse management," said former DSE chairman and broker Khurshid Alam.

Husain was among 36 brokers and company executives implicated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for involvement in share price manipulations that caused upheavals in the market late last year.
"Investors' confidence will return due to the change in the administration. A positive sentiment in the market may push the share prices up," said broker Mohammad Ullah.
The DSE index fell 17.89 points or 1.62 percent at 1,083.79 on turnover of 50 million taka on Sunday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
